topics.name: Phrasal verbs (turn on/off, work out, give in, get out of)
Purpose: so that, in order to, so as to

options: Bach is as famous as Mozart.
Bach is as famous than Mozart.
questions.rule: Equal comparison uses as + adjective + as: as famous as.

options: Please turn of the gramophone now.
Please turn off the gramophone now.
Please turn the gramophone of now.
questions.rule: To stop a machine, we turn it off (off, not 'of').

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: After a past verb (sat), so that is followed by would / could.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: To stop a machine, we switch it off (off, not 'of').

questions.before: He asked me what kind of music
questions.rule: A reported question uses statement order: what kind of music I liked (no did/do).
Comparing one with all the others: the most + long adjective (superlative).
in order to + base verb tells us the purpose of the action.

chat: What did your teacher say about the test?
options: She said that it were easy.
She said me that it was easy.
She said that it was easy.
questions.rule: said that (no person after said); 'it' takes was.

questions.source: Mount Everest is the highest mountain in the world.
options: Mount Everest is higher than any mountain in the world.
Mount Everest is more higher than any other mountain in the world.
Mount Everest is higher than any other mountain in the world.
questions.rule: Superlative to comparative: higher than any other mountain (Everest is not compared with itself).

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 2 errors in this message.
questions.rule: We turn off a fan, and we work out (solve) a problem.

options: He ordered me that sing that back.
He ordered me to sing that back.
He ordered me sing that back.
questions.rule: Reported command: ordered + person + to + base verb.

options: We left early so that we could reach on time.
We left early so that we can reached on time.
We left early so to reach on time.
questions.rule: Past main verb (left) + so that ... could + base verb.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: as ... as takes an adjective: as talented as.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: After asked, can moves back to could.

questions.after: her old toys to the poor children.
questions.rule: give out = hand out to many people. give in = surrender; give off = send out smell or heat.
Before a base verb (look), use in order to. 'So that' needs a subject and verb after it.

questions.prompt: Make a sentence in the comparative degree.
questions.rule: Comparative degree: larger than any other + singular noun.

chat: Why is the room so dark?
options: Sorry, I turned off the lights to save power.
Sorry, I turned of the lights to save power.
Sorry, I turned off the lights for save power.
questions.rule: turned off the lights; purpose is shown with to + base verb (to save).

chat: Which is tastier, a samosa or a pizza?
options: For me, a samosa is tastier than a pizza.
For me, a samosa is more tastier than a pizza.
For me, a samosa is tasty than a pizza.
questions.rule: Short adjective: add -er (tastier). Never use 'more' with an -er word.

questions.source: "You sing very well," Einstein said to me.
options: Einstein told me that you sang very well.
Einstein told me that I sang very well.
Einstein told me that I singed very well.
questions.rule: said to me becomes told me; you becomes I; sing becomes sang.

questions.prompt: Pick the correct positive degree sentence.
options: No other student in the class is brilliant as Tanvi.
No other student in the class is as brilliant as Tanvi.
No other student in the class is as brilliant than Tanvi.
questions.rule: The positive degree needs both parts: as brilliant as.

options: She asked me if was I fond of Bach.
She asked me that if I was fond of Bach.
She asked me if I was fond of Bach.
questions.rule: Yes/no question: asked + if + subject + verb, with no 'that'.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: The main verb is past (played), so use so that ... could.

questions.after: sorry that he had missed so much.
questions.rule: After said, am moves back to was; 'she' takes was, not were.
than needs the comparative: costlier (never 'more costlier').
With a pronoun, the object goes between the parts of the phrasal verb: work it out.

chat: Why are you saving your pocket money?
options: I am saving it so that I could buys a guitar.
I am saving it in order buy a guitar.
I am saving it so that I can buy a guitar.
questions.rule: Present main verb + so that ... can + base verb (buy).

chat: What did the coach tell you?
options: He told me practise for two hours every day.
He told me to practise for two hours every day.
He told me that to practise for two hours every day.
questions.rule: Reported advice or command: told + person + to + verb.

questions.source: Einstein played easy songs first. He wanted the young man to learn step by step.
options: Einstein played easy songs first so that the young man can learnt step by step.
Einstein played easy songs first so that the young man to learn step by step.
Einstein played easy songs first so that the young man could learn step by step.
questions.rule: Past main verb + so that + subject + could + base verb.

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 2 errors in this message.
questions.rule: After asked, the verb moves back: I liked. After to, use the base verb: to sing.

options: You should listen carefully so that you can follow the tune.
You should listens carefully so that you can follow the tune.
You should listen carefully so that you can following the tune.
questions.rule: Modals (should, can) are followed by the base verb: listen, follow.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: One of the + superlative is followed by a plural noun: one of the most beautiful pieces.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Both actions are in the past: got up and came out.
Have heard moves back to had heard after asked; 'we' never takes has.
Reported wh-question: asked + person + what + subject + verb.

chat: Is Pune as big as Mumbai?
options: No, Pune is smaller than Mumbai.
No, Pune is more smaller than Mumbai.
No, Pune is not as bigger as Mumbai.
questions.rule: Use smaller than alone, or not as big as. Don't mix 'more' or 'as' with -er.

options: Not yet. I couldn't worked out the last one.
Not yet. I couldn't work off the last one.
Not yet. I couldn't work out the last one.
questions.rule: work out = solve. After couldn't, use the base verb: work.

questions.source: Her handwriting is better than her sister's.
options: Her sister's handwriting is not as good as hers.
Her sister's handwriting is not as better as hers.
Her sister's handwriting is not as good as her.
questions.rule: better becomes not as good as; compare handwriting with handwriting: hers.

questions.source: Einstein said to me, "Do you remember your first maths lesson?"
options: Einstein asked me if did I remember my first maths lesson.
Einstein asked me if I remembered my first maths lesson.
Einstein asked me if I remembered your first maths lesson.
questions.rule: Yes/no question: asked if + statement order; you/your become I/my; remember becomes remembered.

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 2 errors in this message.
questions.rule: one of the greatest composers (plural). Before than, use the comparative: better.

questions.prompt: Pick the correct indirect speech of: "What a lovely song!" said the boy.
options: The boy exclaimed what a lovely song was it.
The boy exclaimed that it is a very lovely song.
The boy exclaimed that it was a very lovely song.
questions.rule: Exclamation: exclaimed that + statement; 'What a' becomes very, and the tense moves back.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: 'Last night ... arranged' is past, so so that takes could.

questions.before: Very few cities in India are
questions.rule: Positive degree: Very few ... are as + adjective + as ...
Negative purpose: in order not to + base verb ('not' comes before 'to').

chat: Rahul, what did your mother ask you this morning?
options: She asked me whether I had packed my lunch.
She asked me whether had I packed my lunch.
She asked me whether I have pack my lunch.
questions.rule: Reported question: whether + subject + verb; have packed moves back to had packed.

questions.source: The Taj Mahal is more beautiful than any other building in India.
options: The Taj Mahal is the more beautiful building in India.
The Taj Mahal is the most beautiful building in India.
The Taj Mahal is most beautiful building in India.
questions.rule: 'More ... than any other' becomes the most + adjective (with 'the').

questions.source: A diamond is one of the most precious stones.
options: A diamond is more precious than any other stone.
A diamond is more precious than most other stones.
A diamond is more precious than most other stone.
questions.rule: 'One of the most' becomes more ... than most other + plural noun (not 'any other').

questions.source: Einstein said to me, "Just allow yourself to listen."
options: Einstein advised me just to allow yourself to listen.
Einstein advised me that just allow myself to listen.
Einstein advised me just to allow myself to listen.
questions.rule: Advice: advised + person + to + verb; yourself becomes myself.

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 3 errors in this message.
questions.rule: so as not to disturb; in order to teach; past 'tried' + so that ... would.

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 2 errors in this message.
questions.rule: Past story: Einstein got up. give in to = stop resisting and accept something.
